title: Deep-learning chest-radiograph pressure estimates associate with heart-failure prognosis
summary: A post hoc analysis of 534 acute-heart-failure admissions applied a previously developed VGG16-based model to estimate pulmonary arterial wedge pressure from chest radiographs. Higher discharge estimates and smaller decreases during hospitalization were associated with death or heart-failure readmission after adjustment; 223 patients reached the composite endpoint. This single-centre observational analysis does not establish a causal treatment target or improved care. Imaging-view differences and exclusion of in-hospital deaths limit interpretation.

source_review.scope: Primary full article Methods, Results and limitations plus Europe PMC bibliographic metadata; PMC full article.

evidence.tested: Retrospective admission/discharge imaging and adjusted outcome association over median 289 days follow-up.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical utility, multicentre transportability and equivalence across radiograph views remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Previously trained VGG16 regression CNN with global-average-pooling output estimates pressure; model trained on 748 and tested on 188 data in earlier study. Present post hoc 534-patient registry links estimated pressure to outcomes; original prospective registry collection does not establish frozen-model prospective validation.
